\chapter{Learning Theory — Weighted Majority}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.WeightedMajority
\section{Overview}

This module formalizes the mistake-bound analysis of the Weighted Majority algorithm.
Starting from $n$ experts each assigned unit weight, the algorithm multiplies the weight
of every mistaken expert by a penalty factor $\beta \in (0,1)$ after each round.
The key results bound the total number of algorithm mistakes $M_{\mathrm{WM}}$ in terms
of the best expert's mistake count $M^*$ and $n$, and a factor-2 lower bound
shows the analysis is essentially tight for deterministic learners.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Weight shrinkage after $M$ mistakes]
\lean{wm_weight_shrinkage}
\label{wm_weight_shrinkage}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\beta \in (0,1)$, let $W : \bbn \to \bbr$ be a sequence of positive reals, and let
$M$ be a natural number such that $W(k+1) \le W(k) \cdot \tfrac{1+\beta}{2}$ for every
$k < M$. Then
\[
  W(M) \;\le\; W(0) \cdot \left(\frac{1+\beta}{2}\right)^{\!M}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Geometric decay of a shrinking weight sequence]
\lean{wm_weight_upper_bound}
\label{wm_weight_upper_bound}
\leanok
\uses{wm_weight_shrinkage}
\difficulty{1}
Fix an integer $n \ge 1$ and a real number $\beta$ with $0 < \beta < 1$, and let $W
\colon \bbn \to \bbr$ be a sequence of strictly positive reals with $W(0) = n$. Suppose
that for every $k < M$ the sequence shrinks by at least the factor $(1+\beta)/2$ at each
step, in the sense that
\[
  W(k+1) \;\le\; W(k)\cdot\frac{1+\beta}{2}.
\]
Then
\[
  W(M) \;\le\; n\left(\frac{1+\beta}{2}\right)^{\!M}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Combined potential bound in logarithmic form]
\lean{wm_combined_potential_bound}
\label{wm_combined_potential_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
Let $\beta \in (0,1)$ and let $n \ge 1$ be an integer, and let $M^\ast, M_{\mathrm{WM}}$
be nonnegative integers satisfying
\[
  \beta^{M^\ast} \;\le\; n \cdot \left(\tfrac{1+\beta}{2}\right)^{M_{\mathrm{WM}}}.
\]
Then
\[
  \log\!\left(\beta^{M^\ast}\right)
  \;\le\;
  \log\!\left(n \cdot \left(\tfrac{1+\beta}{2}\right)^{M_{\mathrm{WM}}}\right),
\]
where $\log$ denotes the natural logarithm.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Logarithmic mistake bound]
\lean{wm_mistake_bound_log}
\label{wm_mistake_bound_log}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer and let $\beta \in (0,1)$. Suppose $M^*$ and
$M_{\mathrm{WM}}$ are nonnegative integers satisfying
\[
  \beta^{M^*} \;\le\; n \cdot \left(\frac{1+\beta}{2}\right)^{M_{\mathrm{WM}}}.
\]
Then
\[
  M_{\mathrm{WM}} \cdot \log\!\frac{2}{1+\beta}
  \;\le\;
  \log n \;+\; M^* \cdot \log\frac{1}{\beta}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Factor-2 mistake bound for a deterministic learner]
\lean{deterministic_factor2_lower_bound}
\label{deterministic_factor2_lower_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $T$ there exist natural numbers $M_{\mathrm{alg}}$ and $M^*$
such that $M_{\mathrm{alg}} = T$ and $2M^* \le T$. Interpreting $M_{\mathrm{alg}}$ as
the number of mistakes made by a deterministic online learner over $T$ rounds and $M^*$
as the number made by the best fixed expert, this exhibits a scenario in which the
learner errs on every round while the best expert errs at most $T/2$ times, so no
deterministic strategy can guarantee fewer than twice the optimal number of mistakes.
\end{theorem}
